walk/start: To make a new image, run the noising backwards. Start at the last step, a thousand, where an image is pure noise: just draw x t from a standard normal.
walk/loop: Then walk back one step at a time, down to zero, removing a little noise each time.
walk/call: Each step asks the network once for its noise guess. A thousand steps, a thousand network calls.
step/guess: Here is one step, from t down to t minus one. Say alpha bar t is zero point six four, a pixel reads zero point five, and the network guesses its noise is minus a half.
step/est: First, estimate the clean image, as before: take away zero point six times the guess, and divide by zero point eight. x zero hat is one.
step/back: Then blend it back in, one step down, where alpha bar t minus one is zero point eight one. Its square root, zero point nine, scales x zero hat.
step/split: That leaves zero point one nine for noise. Set sigma squared of it aside for fresh noise, here zero point zero three. The other zero point one six goes to the guess, scaled by its root, zero point four.
step/mean: So the step's mean is zero point nine times one, plus zero point four times minus a half: zero point seven.
step/fresh: Last, add sigma times fresh noise z, from a standard normal. With z equal to one, x t minus one is zero point seven plus zero point one seven: zero point eight seven.
end/why: Why add noise while taking it away? The mean is only the center of where the step could land. Fresh noise picks one point around it, and refills the noise share that step t minus one should have.
end/last: On the last step, down to zero, alpha bar is one: no noise share is left. Nothing of the guess is kept, nothing fresh is added, and the image is the estimate x zero hat itself.
end/count: So a thousand steps take a thousand network calls, but only nine hundred and ninety nine fresh draws.
end/skip: And since the blend can land on any level, a sampler can also skip: a thousand, nine eighty, nine sixty, and so on. Fifty calls instead of a thousand.
